title: Why ME/CFS Isn’t Just Tiredness: A Psychologist Breaks It Down

sentences.zh: 患有肌痛性脑脊髓炎（ME）或慢性疲劳综合征（CFS）究竟是一种怎样的体验？

sentences.en: In this episode, my guest, Dr. Beth, shares her personal experience of managing this often misunderstood condition.
sentences.zh: 在本期节目中，我的嘉宾贝丝博士将分享她应对这种常被误解的疾病的个人经历。

sentences.en: From what a bad day really looks like to treatment options that can actually help.

sentences.zh: 让我们开始吧，一起来听听我和贝丝博士的对话，我们在节目另一头见。

sentences.en: Hi, Beth.
sentences.zh: 嗨，贝丝。

sentences.en: So lovely to have you along.
sentences.zh: 很高兴你能来。

sentences.en: Thank you for being here.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你来到这里。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for having me.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我。

sentences.en: And thank you especially for being here, because I know with your condition, it means that, you know, you have to choose where to spend your energy.
sentences.zh: 尤其要谢谢你能来，因为我知道鉴于你的身体状况，这意味着你需要有所选择地消耗精力。

sentences.en: So thank you for sharing some of your energy with our audience.
sentences.zh: 所以谢谢你与我们的听众分享你的一部分精力。

sentences.en: You're very welcome.
sentences.zh: 不用客气。

sentences.en: So before we begin, could you tell us what ME forward slash CFS is?
sentences.zh: 那么在我们开始之前，你能告诉我们什么是ME斜杠CFS吗？

sentences.en: I can, and I can try and pronounce it as best to my ability, but they do make it very difficult by giving them long medical terMs.
sentences.zh: 可以的，我会尽我最大努力把它读出来，但它们起了这么长的医学术语，确实让人很难念。

sentences.en: So ME is myalgic encephalomyelitis, also known as chronic fatigue syndrome or CFS or ME.
sentences.zh: 所以，ME是肌痛性脑脊髓炎（Myalgic Encephalomyelitis），也被称为慢性疲劳综合征、CFS或ME。

sentences.en: And it's often thought of as just feeling tired.
sentences.zh: 人们通常认为它只是感觉疲劳。

sentences.en: And that's largely due to the chronic fatigue syndrome title that has given it that misconception.
sentences.zh: 这主要归咎于“慢性疲劳综合征”这个名字，它造成了这种误解。

sentences.en: But actually, it's quite a complex and chronic neurological illness that can affect the brain, the nervous system.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，这是一种相当复杂且慢性的神经系统疾病，会影响大脑和神经系统。

sentences.en: And now they're even looking down to a cellular mitochondria level.
sentences.zh: 现在他们甚至开始研究到细胞线粒体的层面。

sentences.en: But the main features that you will tend to see are fatigue, unrefreshing sleep.
sentences.zh: 但你往往会看到的主要特征是疲劳、睡眠无法恢复精力。

sentences.en: No matter how much sleep you've had, you don't wake feeling refreshed from the night before.
sentences.zh: 无论你睡了多久，醒来时都不会觉得前晚的疲惫得到了恢复。

sentences.en: We have what we call post-exertional malaise, also known as PEM, which we could talk a little bit more about.
sentences.zh: 我们有一种叫做“劳累后不适”的症状，也称为PEM，我们可以多聊聊这个。

sentences.en: Cognitive impairments like brain fog or concentration or forgetfulness, pain.
sentences.zh: 认知障碍，比如脑雾、注意力不集中或健忘，以及疼痛。

sentences.en: And there's also a crossover with orthostatic intolerance.
sentences.zh: 此外，它还与直立不耐受存在交叉重叠。

sentences.en: So people's blood flow not behaving as it should.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，人们的血液流动表现得不如预期。

sentences.en: So I'm also diagnosed with POTS, which is postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome.
sentences.zh: 所以我也被诊断患有POTS，即体位性心动过速综合征。

sentences.en: So yet more technical terms,
sentences.zh: 又是一些专业术语，

sentences.en: which basically means that my heart and my blood flow doesn't do what it should do when I am standing up or when I am walking around the way it does with somebody without orthostatic intolerances.
sentences.zh: 这基本上意味着，当我站起来或四处走动时，我的心脏和血液流动不像没有直立不耐受的人那样正常运作。

sentences.en: And it's quite a tricky diagnosis to receive because there's no tests for it.
sentences.zh: 这是一个相当棘手的诊断，因为没有针对它的检测方法。

sentences.en: So it's a diagnosis of exclusion where everything else that you can possibly think of has been ruled out probably over a number of years before you're finally given the diagnosis.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个排除性诊断，在最终确诊之前，可能需要经过好几年，将所有你能想到的其他可能性都排除掉。

sentences.en: And what we know now is that it frequently follows in some people a viral infection where the body hasn't fully recovered.
sentences.zh: 我们现在所知道的是，在某些人身上，它经常继发于病毒感染，此时身体尚未完全恢复。

sentences.en: And that's what happened in my case.
sentences.zh: 这就是我身上的情况。

sentences.en: And it's now what we're seeing with COVID and long COVID as well.
sentences.zh: 这也是我们在新冠肺炎以及长新冠（Long COVID）中看到的情况。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I guess I was definitely thinking about the parallels.
sentences.zh: 我想我确实在思考其中的相似之处。

sentences.en: And I think long COVID, it feels like long COVID is more accepted and more validated.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为长新冠，感觉长新冠更容易被接受、更有正当性。

sentences.en: Whereas with ME, I feel like there is more stigma.
sentences.zh: 然而对于ME，我感觉存在更多污名化。

sentences.en: But I'm talking about that as a mental health professional and as kind of perhaps knowing people have had ME.
sentences.zh: 但我是作为一名心理健康专业人士，并且可能因为认识得ME的人而这么说。

sentences.en: That might feel quite different when you are a psychologist and you have a diagnosis of ME.
sentences.zh: 当你本身是一名心理学家又被诊断出患有ME时，感觉可能会很不相同。

sentences.en: Could you talk to me about stigma and kind of, you know, what people say about it or think about it?
sentences.zh: 你能跟我谈谈污名化以及人们对此说些什么或有何看法吗？

sentences.en: This isn't just, you know, I've not long had lunch.
sentences.zh: 这可不仅仅是，你知道的，我刚吃完午饭不久。

sentences.en: This isn't just, oh, I'm having the post-lunch slump, is it?
sentences.zh: 这可不只是那种“哦，我正经历午后倦怠”的状态，对吧？

sentences.en: But I think perhaps some people think it is that.
sentences.zh: 但我想有些人可能认为它就是那样。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全如此。

sentences.en: I think people just see it as feeling a bit tired or needing more reSt.
sentences.zh: 我认为人们只把它看作是感觉有点累，或者需要多休息。

sentences.en: And it's so much more complicated than that.
sentences.zh: 但它要复杂得多。

sentences.en: So, you know, mild version of ME might look like a little bit more rest, extra rest in between activities.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，轻度ME可能表现为在活动之间稍微多休息一下。

sentences.en: But it can also be managing that cognitive fog.
sentences.zh: 但它也可能需要应对那种认知脑雾。

sentences.en: It can be mobility difficulties that somebody finds it hard to get around, limiting activities.
sentences.zh: 它可能是行动不便，让人觉得四处走动很困难，从而限制了活动。

sentences.en: All the way to the severe end of ME where somebody can be bedbound because they don't have the energy or the capacity to lift their body out of the bed.
sentences.zh: 一直到严重程度的ME，患者可能会卧床不起，因为他们没有力气或能力将身体撑起离开床铺。

sentences.en: They can't tolerate light or sound.
sentences.zh: 他们无法忍受光线或声音。

sentences.en: They might require full-time care.
sentences.zh: 他们可能需要全天候的护理。

sentences.en: And I think you're right.
sentences.zh: 我想你说得对。

sentences.en: There is difference in the stigma towards long COVID than there is ME.
sentences.zh: 对长新冠的污名化与对ME的污名化是有区别的。

sentences.en: And possibly that's because of the times that we're in where ME was called yuppie flu in the 80s.
sentences.zh: 这可能是因为我们所处的时代不同，ME在80年代曾被称为“雅皮士流感”。

sentences.en: And it was looked at as more kind of laziness.
sentences.zh: 当时它被看作是一种比较懒惰的表现。

sentences.en: Whereas with the long COVID, there's been so much more research done to show the effects of COVID and post-viral fatigue.
sentences.zh: 而对于长新冠，已经做了更多的研究来展示新冠病毒和病毒后疲劳的影响。

sentences.en: Yeah, thank you for illuminating us on that.
sentences.zh: 是的，谢谢你对此为我们做出的阐释。

sentences.en: And I think until really meeting with you today, even, I hadn't appreciated how it can be, you know, psychological, physical, like everything, identity.
sentences.zh: 我想直到今天真正见到你之前，我甚至都没有意识到它可以是心理上的、身体上的，方方面面的，甚至是关乎身份认同的。

sentences.en: I guess even because it's not necessarily something that people are born with.
sentences.zh: 我想甚至因为这不一定是人们生来就有的东西。

sentences.en: It's something that they have to adapt to.
sentences.zh: 这是他们不得不去适应的东西。

sentences.en: And perhaps the people and the systems and maybe even the work or occupational environments around you perhaps no longer fit or people's expectations of you.
sentences.zh: 或许你身边的人、系统，甚至工作或职业环境，可能不再适合你，或者人们对你的期望不再匹配。

sentences.en: Maybe, you know, they miss the old you, but you likely also really miss the old you too.
sentences.zh: 也许，你知道的，他们怀念以前的你，但你大概也非常怀念以前的自己。

sentences.en: Like it's a whole sea change, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 就像是一场翻天覆地的巨变，对吧？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And it impacts on every part of somebody's life.
sentences.zh: 它会影响一个人生活的方方面面。

sentences.en: It's not just on one part.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是某一个方面。

sentences.en: It's work.
sentences.zh: 是工作。

sentences.en: It's education.
sentences.zh: 是教育。

sentences.en: It might impact on how much you can do.
sentences.zh: 它可能会影响你能做多少事情。

sentences.en: It might impact on the type of work that you can do.
sentences.zh: 它可能会影响你能从事的工作类型。

sentences.en: And obviously at the severe end, people aren't able to work at all.
sentences.zh: 显然在严重的情况下，人们根本无法工作。

sentences.en: And the person that you were before, it might not be the person that you can be now.
sentences.zh: 以前的那个你，可能不再是现在的你能成为的那个你了。

sentences.en: So prior to my diagnosis, I was always described as busy, you know, working full time in the NHS and weightlifting four or five times a week.
sentences.zh: 所以在确诊之前，我总是被形容为是个大忙人，你知道的，在NHS全职工作，一周举重四到五次。

sentences.en: And then my hobbies on top and then my socializing on top.
sentences.zh: 此外还有我的业余爱好，以及各种社交活动。

sentences.en: And all of that busy identity has to change and adapt.
sentences.zh: 所有这些忙碌的身份都必须改变和适应。

sentences.en: And the people around you have to also adapt to those changes too.
sentences.zh: 你周围的人也必须适应这些变化。

sentences.en: And recognize that you have these energy limitations and there can be a lot of grief for not only the life that you have lost,
sentences.zh: 并且要认识到你有这些能量限制，不仅会为失去的生活感到悲伤，

sentences.en: but also the life that you had planned and thought that you would have might now look very different.
sentences.zh: 还会为原本计划好、以为自己会拥有的生活现在可能看起来大不相同而感到遗憾。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's kind of reminding me that when I was at uni, I think we studied multiple sclerosis
sentences.zh: 是的，这让我想起我在大学时，我们似乎研究过多发性硬化症，

sentences.en: and there was some evidence that people with a type A personality were more likely to get an MS diagnosis.
sentences.zh: 并且有一些证据表明，A型性格的人更有可能被诊断出患有MS（多发性硬化症）。

sentences.en: Do you know if there's any correlation for any traits in ME and CFS?
sentences.zh: 你知道ME和CFS是否存在任何性格特质上的相关性吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, there does seem to be some trends with perfectionist types, the people who probably are going to get an infection
sentences.zh: 是的，完美主义倾向的人似乎确实存在一些趋势，这些人可能在感染病毒后，

sentences.en: and then don't take the time to recover because they're so keen to return to work.
sentences.zh: 却不花时间去恢复，因为他们太渴望回到工作岗位了。

sentences.en: And that was, you know, speaking from my experience, that is definitely what happened with me,
sentences.zh: 而且，（从我的经历来说），我身上绝对就是这样发生的，

sentences.en: where I had a viral infection of some sort, but, you know, that couldn't stand in the way of work.
sentences.zh: 当时我感染了某种病毒，但是，你知道的，那不能成为工作路上的绊脚石。

sentences.en: I had to get back to work and see my clients and rush back too soon and then obviously became unwell again.
sentences.zh: 我必须重返工作岗位，看诊我的客户，过早地匆忙回去，然后很明显又生病了。

sentences.en: And later down the line, this has obviously impacted my nervous system somehow.
sentences.zh: 而在后来，这显然以某种方式影响了我的神经系统。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I think, you know, the audience listening to or watching this will be doing so either because they are struggling with these symptoms
sentences.zh: 我想，收听或观看这个节目的听众，要么是因为他们正在与这些症状作斗争，

sentences.en: or they care about someone or they are working in mental health.
sentences.zh: 要么是因为他们关心某人，要么是从事心理健康工作。

sentences.en: And so, you know, I think especially when we are kind of caregivers, we can often feel that pressure to hurry back
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，我认为特别是当我们扮演照顾者的角色时，我们经常会感到那种催促自己快点回去的压力，

sentences.en: before we're fully ready because we don't want to let people down or we've got to support the team or, you know, everyone else is off kind of on long-term sick, you know.
sentences.zh: 在完全准备好之前就回去，因为我们不想让人失望，或者我们必须支持团队，或者，你知道的，其他人都去请长期病假了，你知道的。

sentences.en: And it's, you know, we can understand these pressures, but actually really thinking about when I've had sick leave,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，我们能理解这些压力，但实际上真正思考当我请过病假时，

sentences.en: am I fully ready to return, not to light duties, but am I fully ready to do my job?
sentences.zh: 我是不是真的完全准备好回去了，不是说去做轻松的活，而是我真的完全准备好胜任我的工作了吗？

sentences.en: And I often think even when I've had a cold or I've had, you know, a vomit bug or something, even after the exclusion period where I'm technically allowed back,
sentences.zh: 我经常觉得，即使我感冒了，或者得了呕吐病之类的，甚至在过了医学上允许我返岗的隔离期之后，

sentences.en: I think you always need a day of being out of bed and kind of mobilising, you know, from your sofa to your kitchen and back again.
sentences.zh: 我想你总是需要有一天能够下床活动，比如从沙发走到厨房再走回来。

sentences.en: But then you also need an extra day to really strengthen your body and your mind because it reminds me of when I'd broken my arm two years ago
sentences.zh: 但随后你还需要额外的一天来真正强健你的身体和心智，因为这让我想起两年前我摔断手臂时，

sentences.en: and the physio told me afterwards that even kind of as short as a couple of days in bed
sentences.zh: 理疗师事后告诉我，哪怕在床上躺短短几天，

sentences.en: gives the body the message, actually, we're wasting energy by continuing to fuel these muscles.
sentences.zh: 也会给身体传递这样一个信号：实际上，继续为这些肌肉提供能量是在浪费能量。

sentences.en: And so it tries to preserve its energy by stripping that energy back from the tendons, which means that your tendons start to contract.
sentences.zh: 因此，它试图通过从肌腱中抽回能量来保存能量，这意味着你的肌腱开始收缩。

sentences.en: And she said that if you're not getting out of bed, if you're not doing things, if you're not flexing your body, it then takes a whole lot more effort to stretch them again.
sentences.zh: 她说，如果你不经常下床，如果你不做事情，如果你不活动身体，那么重新拉伸它们就需要付出更多的努力。

sentences.en: It's not two days.
sentences.zh: 这可不止两天。

sentences.en: This might be weeks or months if you've been in bed for a week or four, for example.
sentences.zh: 如果你在床上躺了一个星期或四周，这可能需要数周或数月。

sentences.en: And, you know, if you're resting a lot, then your body is constantly getting the message, oh, we don't need to power these legs.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，如果你躺着休息很多，那么你的身体就会不断收到信号：哦，我们不需要给这些腿供能。

sentences.en: We don't need to have that available.
sentences.zh: 我们不需要保持这种体能。

sentences.en: And, you know, I think to cut a very long rambling story short, when we're going back to work, we really need to make sure that we are mobilising normally,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，为了长话短说，当我们重返工作岗位时，我们真的需要确保我们能正常活动，

sentences.en: that we are really up to speed, that, you know, that our brain fog has lifted enough to be able to sit with clients and not having to be constantly wiping our nose
sentences.zh: 确保我们的状态真正恢复，你知道的，我们的脑雾已经消散到足以坐在客户面前，而不需要不停地擦鼻子

sentences.en: or thinking about ourselves.
sentences.zh: 或者满脑子只想着自己。

sentences.en: And we've got to be well when we return to work.
sentences.zh: 在我们重返工作岗位时，我们必须是真正健康的。

sentences.en: And actually, that will stay with me now even more, thinking about we deserve to reSt.
sentences.zh: 实际上，这会让我铭记在心，甚至思考我们理应休息。

sentences.en: And actually, our future self, which then hopefully wouldn't get a condition like this, would thank us for that.
sentences.zh: 并且实际上，我们未来的自己（希望到时不会得这种病）会为此感谢我们的。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And I think that is a huge thing that we need to recognise within this hustle culture that we're in.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是我们在当今这种内卷文化中需要意识到的巨大问题。

sentences.en: And I remember one of the nurses that I was working with at the time said to me, if you're not careful, you're going to get post-viral fatigue.
sentences.zh: 我记得当时和我一起工作的一位护士对我说：“如果你不小心，你会得病毒后疲劳的。”

sentences.en: And I just didn't consider the long-term outcome that going back to work, which sounds so simple, could have had.
sentences.zh: 而我当时根本没有考虑到重返工作岗位（听起来那么简单）可能会带来的长期后果。

sentences.en: But if I had heard that advice back then, perhaps I wouldn't have rushed back as quickly as I did.
sentences.zh: 但如果我当时听了那个建议，或许我就不会像当时那样急着回去了。

sentences.en: Amazing.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: And I think especially when we're working for the NHS, we have to know that we can have, usually, up to six months on full pay.
sentences.zh: 而且我想，特别是当我们为NHS工作时，我们必须知道我们通常可以享有长达六个月的全薪病假。

sentences.en: Not always.
sentences.zh: 并非总是如此。

sentences.en: And we wouldn't necessarily encourage people to take sick leave that didn't need it.
sentences.zh: 我们也不一定鼓励不需要的人去请病假。

sentences.en: But I know that even more recently, there's been kind of counting episodes of sick leave.
sentences.zh: 但我知道，更近一点的时候，有一种对病假次数的统计方式。

sentences.en: And people are only allowed so many episodes in a year.
sentences.zh: 人们一年内只被允许请那么多次病假。

sentences.en: But I still would say, if you've had the episode because you've been unwell, you might as well make sure that you are well.
sentences.zh: 但我还是要说，如果你因为生病而请了假，你最好确保自己已经彻底康复了。

sentences.en: Because certainly in the NHS, it's not necessarily the days that are counted, it is the episode.
sentences.zh: 因为在NHS，计算的往往不是天数，而是请假的次数。

sentences.en: So get yourself well.
sentences.zh: 所以，先把自己的身体养好。

sentences.en: That was really good advice.
sentences.zh: 这真的是一个很好的建议。

sentences.en: But at that time, I guess you couldn't heed it.
sentences.zh: 但在当时，我想你可能听不进去。

sentences.en: Maybe it felt irritating or silly.
sentences.zh: 也许觉得很烦人，或者很蠢。

sentences.en: How did that feel when she said that?
sentences.zh: 她那样说的时候，你有什么感觉？

sentences.en: It felt like an exaggeration or perhaps overprotective or it just didn't seem real to me at that point
sentences.zh: 感觉像是一种夸大，或者可能过于保护，或者在那个时候对我来说显得很不真实，

sentences.en: that something that you just deal with, you know, like a flu or a glandular fever or a bug,
sentences.zh: 就好像那是你只需要去应付的事情，你知道的，就像流感、腺热或者小毛病一样，

sentences.en: you know, we just think, you know, that's what happens in life and you just go back to normality.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们只会觉得，这就是生活中会发生的事，然后你就会回归正常。

sentences.en: So it just didn't feel within my, I guess, my headspace at that time that that was actually important.
sentences.zh: 所以当时我根本没觉得，我想，在我的意识里这有什么重要的。

sentences.en: And although that that virus was 2015, 2016, I think around there, my symptoms of ME didn't actually start to show up until 2020.
sentences.zh: 尽管那个病毒是2015、2016年左右的事，我记不清了，但我肌痛性脑脊髓炎（ME）的症状实际上直到2020年才开始显现。

sentences.en: You know, whatever was going on internally was just sitting in the background there until it became so difficult that it would start to show up and present itself.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，无论体内在发生什么，它就只是潜伏在后台，直到变得如此严重，以至于开始显现并表现出来。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。

sentences.en: And I'm sorry to hear how long you've struggled with this.
sentences.zh: 听到你与此抗争了这么久，我感到很遗憾。

sentences.en: Just to help us to kind of paint a picture, would you be able to give us an idea about perhaps what a bad day looks like for somebody with this diagnosis?
sentences.zh: 为了帮我们大致了解一下，你能否向我们描述一下，被诊断为这种病的人糟糕的一天是怎样的？

sentences.en: I can.
sentences.zh: 我可以的。

sentences.en: It's one of those diagnosis where everybody is so different, depending on where they are on the kind of mild to severe spectrum,
sentences.zh: 这是一种因人而异的诊断，取决于他们在轻度到重度光谱上的位置，

sentences.en: but also in the types of symptoms that they get because everybody's symptoms are so different.
sentences.zh: 同时也取决于他们所患症状的类型，因为每个人的症状都大不相同。

sentences.en: So some people might not be able to get out of the bed, might not be able to shower, might not be able to use the bathroom, you know, make a meal.
sentences.zh: 所以有些人可能无法下床，可能无法洗澡，可能无法使用洗手间，你知道的，无法做饭。

sentences.en: They might have to block out light from their room if it's becoming too much sensory overload.
sentences.zh: 如果感官超载太严重，他们可能不得不把房间的灯光遮挡起来。

sentences.en: Other people might just, I say just, like it's simple, it's not.
sentences.zh: 其他人可能只是——我说“只是”，好像很简单似的，其实一点也不。

sentences.en: Other people might need to plan breaks.
sentences.zh: 其他人可能需要规划休息时间。

sentences.en: They might need to take themselves away from loud environments.
sentences.zh: 他们可能需要让自己远离嘈杂的环境。

sentences.en: Myself, a difficult day can look like pain.
sentences.zh: 对我自己而言，艰难的一天可能表现为疼痛。

sentences.en: So I get pain more than I get fatigue, whereas other people can get fatigue more than they get pain.
sentences.zh: 所以我经历的疼痛比疲劳多，而其他人经历的疲劳可能比疼痛多。

sentences.en: It's just different in how it presents itself.
sentences.zh: 只是表现形式各不相同。

sentences.en: And then I can have a few months where I'll have a sore throat every day and then that passes.
sentences.zh: 然后我可能会有几个月每天都喉咙痛，接着就会过去。

sentences.en: And then I'll have a few months where I have nausea every day and then that passes.
sentences.zh: 然后我会有几个月每天都恶心，接着就会过去。

sentences.en: And I don't know why it changes, but it does.
sentences.zh: 我不知道为什么会变，但它确实会变。

sentences.en: I only ever really get the fatigue part of this diagnosis if I'm heading towards a crash, towards the post-exertional malaise.
sentences.zh: 只有当我走向崩溃、走向活动后不适（PEM）时，我才会真正体验到这种诊断带来的疲劳部分。

sentences.en: That's the only time I'll really feel the fatigue.
sentences.zh: 那是唯一让我真正感到疲劳的时候。

sentences.en: And it's like having the flu in that you feel heavy and you have no energy just without the snots and the coughs.
sentences.zh: 这就好比得了流感，你会感到沉重、精疲力竭，只是没有流鼻涕和咳嗽。

sentences.en: But that physical feeling is the same.
sentences.zh: 但那种身体上的感觉是一样的。

sentences.en: I can also pick up infections very easily, which is something that I didn't know until I had it,
sentences.zh: 我也很容易感染，这是我得病前不知道的，

sentences.en: in that my immune system doesn't protect me in the same way that somebody without this diagnosis might have.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，我的免疫系统不像没有这种诊断的人那样保护我。

sentences.en: So that requires being quite careful around people.
sentences.zh: 所以这要求在与人接触时必须相当小心。

sentences.en: And if I do pick up an infection, I don't quite recover like I used to.
sentences.zh: 如果我真的感染了，我就没法像以前那样恢复了。

sentences.en: It takes a lot longer.
sentences.zh: 需要花费长得多的时间。

sentences.en: Forgetfulness, brain fog.
sentences.zh: 健忘，脑雾。

sentences.en: I suppose some people might feel the emotional side of having all of these different symptoMs.
sentences.zh: 我想有些人可能会感受到拥有所有这些不同症状带来的情绪影响。

sentences.en: You know, it's not just physical.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这不仅仅是身体上的。

sentences.en: It's not just the cognitive symptoMs.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是认知症状。

sentences.en: It's then dealing with them.
sentences.zh: 然后还要应对这些症状。

sentences.en: And grief is a part of that, like I've already mentioned.
sentences.zh: 正如我刚才已经提到的，悲伤也是其中的一部分。

sentences.en: A massive amount of apathy.
sentences.zh: 大量的冷漠感。

sentences.en: You know, if you're tired, normally you don't have motivation and you don't want to do things.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，如果你累了，通常你就没有动力，也不想做事。

sentences.en: And so when you're in a crash, it's very difficult to feel like you can be bothered about most things until you can come out the other side of that crash.
sentences.zh: 所以当处于崩溃状态时，你很难觉得自己能对大多数事情上心，直到你能走出那种崩溃状态。

sentences.en: And the frustration at being held back from the things that you want to do, but either know that you can't or that you shouldn't for now.
sentences.zh: 还有那种被阻止去做自己想做的事所带来的挫败感，但你又明知自己做不到，或者目前不应该去做。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think even the identity around yourself and your relationship to work.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为甚至还涉及到你对自我的认同以及你与工作的关系。

sentences.en: I know I would find that really challenging adjusting because I often say psychology for me feels different.
sentences.zh: 我知道我会觉得调整起来非常具有挑战性，因为我经常说，心理学对我的感觉是不一样的。

sentences.en: So I might say to my children or my husband, oh, I'd rather stay in bed and read my book, especially because I'm reading a really good book at the moment.
sentences.zh: 所以我可能会对我的孩子或丈夫说，哦，我宁愿呆在床上看书，特别是由于我最近正在看一本非常好的书。

sentences.en: But whenever I'm with a client or doing something like this, like I really love it.
sentences.zh: 但每当我和客户在一起或者做像这样切身的事情时，我是真的很喜欢。

sentences.en: And is that something that's different?
sentences.zh: 这有什么不同吗？

sentences.en: Like you can't almost switch on the gear that you'd used to be able to kind of keep in the tank.
sentences.zh: 就好像你几乎无法开启你以前能够储存在体内的那种档位。

sentences.en: Do you know what I mean?
sentences.zh: 你知道我的意思吗？

sentences.en: To be able to to give your best to your work.
sentences.zh: 为了能够把最好的一面奉献给你的工作。

sentences.en: To be able to do that, it has to be very carefully planned.
sentences.zh: 为了做到这一点，必须经过非常仔细的规划。

sentences.en: So I have to think about rest breaks.
sentences.zh: 所以我必须考虑休息时间。

sentences.en: I have to think about how many people in a day.
sentences.zh: 我必须考虑一天见多少人。

sentences.en: I have to think about if I'm seeing that person, what am I doing after that?
sentences.zh: 我必须考虑如果我要见那个人，我之后要做什么？

sentences.en: What am I doing before that?
sentences.zh: 我之前要做什么？

sentences.en: Have I eaten?
sentences.zh: 我吃过东西了吗？

sentences.en: Have I hydrated?
sentences.zh: 我补充水分了吗？

sentences.en: So it just takes a lot more forethought than I used to have to do.
sentences.zh: 所以这比我过去需要做的要多得多深思熟虑。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And it's reminding me of trying to sort out, you know, it's going to be a real nightmare trying to sort out with your mates when you're actually going to meet up.
sentences.zh: 这让我想起试着去安排，你知道的，当你和死党们约定究竟什么时候见面时，那绝对会是一场噩梦。

sentences.en: If you will live in different parts of the country.
sentences.zh: 如果你住在国家的不同地方的话。

sentences.en: Frankly, if you all live in the same part of the country, it's still a nightmare.
sentences.zh: 坦白说，如果你都住在国家的同一个地方，那依然是一场噩梦。

sentences.en: Modern life's right.
sentences.zh: 现代生活就是这样。

sentences.en: But I was looking through my diary and I was like,
sentences.zh: 但我翻看日记时，我就在想：

sentences.en: I can't do that weekend because actually I've got Simply Red and then the next day I've got a calligraphy course and then I'm going out for dinner the next day.
sentences.zh: 我那个周末去不了，因为实际上我要看“红唇合唱团（Simply Red）”的演出，然后第二天我有书法课，接着第二天我要出去吃晚饭。

sentences.en: You, I guess, would kind of probably not choose to do three activities like that altogether.
sentences.zh: 我想，你大概不会选择把这样三项活动排在一起。

sentences.en: But also how is it to look ahead and book anything and put money on the line for things that you may or may not be able to do ultimately?
sentences.zh: 但同时，展望未来并预订任何事情，为那些你最终可能做也可能做不到的事情压上真金白银，感觉又会怎样呢？

sentences.en: Yeah, I can't tell you the amount of concerts, gigs,
sentences.zh: 是的，我无法告诉你我有多少次演唱会、演出、

sentences.en: theatre tickets that I've just had to write off or try and last minute resell because it's not something that you can totally have control over.
sentences.zh: 戏剧门票不得不直接作废，或者尝试在最后一刻转手，因为这不是一件你能完全掌控的事情。

sentences.en: You know, I can plan until the cows come home.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我可以筹划到天荒地老。

sentences.en: You know, I can really put thought into what that week looks like if I've got an activity.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，如果我有一项活动，我真的可以深思熟虑地规划那一周看起来会是怎样。

sentences.en: But it's what it is on the day.
sentences.zh: 但关键在于当天的情况如何。

sentences.en: You know, some days that planning pays off and some days the body has other ideas and says, no, does make you kind of a flaky person that you have to cancel last minute,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，有时那种规划会有回报，有时身体会有别的想法并说“不”，这确实会让你成为那种不得不临时取消行程的“不靠谱”的人，

sentences.en: which I never have been.
sentences.zh: 我以前从来都不是这样的人。

sentences.en: But I think there's perhaps, you know, flaky gets a bad reputation, really, or it's not the most appropriate word here.
sentences.zh: 但我想也许，你知道的，“不靠谱”名声不太好，或者在这里它并不是最贴切的词。

sentences.en: It's that you, you're unwell.
sentences.zh: 情况是这样的，你生病了。

sentences.en: You can't do it.
sentences.zh: 你做不到。

sentences.en: You know, if you'd suddenly come down with a vomit bug, people would understand, wouldn't they?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，如果你突然染上了呕吐胃肠炎，大家都会理解的，对吧？

sentences.en: But I guess it's, oh, you know, how many times is Beth going to say she's tired?
sentences.zh: 但我想情况是，“哦，你知道的，贝丝要说多少次她很累？”

sentences.en: But actually, that's really, that's really dismissive, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 但实际上，这真的很，真的很轻视人，不是吗？

sentences.en: And that's not fully embracing you or embracing the person with this condition.
sentences.zh: 而且这并没有完全包容你，也没有包容患有这种疾病的人。

sentences.en: And actually, we need to get over ourselves, really, and think, well, how can I support Beth?
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们真的需要克服自我中心，想一想，嗯，我该如何支持贝丝？

sentences.en: You know, perhaps rather than going out for dinner, perhaps if I was to say, can I bring us dinner?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，也许与其出去吃晚饭，不如我提议：“我把晚饭带过去好吗？”

sentences.en: And, you know, perhaps we make sure we're finished by 8 p.m.
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道的，也许我们确保在晚上8点前结束。

sentences.en: Would that feel OK?
sentences.zh: 这样感觉可以吗？

sentences.en: Or is that not OK?
sentences.zh: 还是说这样不行？

sentences.en: But I want to see you.
sentences.zh: 但我很想见你。

sentences.en: I want to spend time with you.
sentences.zh: 我想花时间和你在一起。

sentences.en: But I want to meet you where you are.
sentences.zh: 但我想要迁就你的现状。

sentences.en: Is that kind of a helpful accommodation?
sentences.zh: 这算是一种有用的体谅和迁就吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And actually, my friends are so understanding and so supportive in that our relationships have had to be very much text-based now.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我的朋友们非常理解也极其支持，以至于我们的关系现在不得不基本上依靠发信息来维持。

sentences.en: You know, we'll send memes, we'll send GIFs, you know, we'll do things like that, that I can stay in touch and I can do whilst resting.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们会发表情包、发动图，你知道的，我们会做诸如此类的事情，这样我既能保持联系，又能在休息的同时做到这一点。

sentences.en: And there's lots of accommodations.
sentences.zh: 而且有很多体谅和迁就的方式。

sentences.en: So people will either come to me rather than going for a walk like we used to, or I met up with a friend the other week for a coffee and it was, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以大家要么会来找我，而不是像以前那样去散步，或者前几周我和一个朋友见面喝咖啡，当时我就在想，

sentences.en: thinking about where we sit there that's not going to be too loud.
sentences.zh: 考虑我们坐在哪里才不会太吵。

sentences.en: So I don't have to overly concentrate on trying to hear her while they're banging the coffee grinders together.
sentences.zh: 这样我就不必过度集中注意力去努力听她说话，同时旁边还在发出咖啡研磨机的轰鸣声。

sentences.en: And also her accommodation was so lovely that she checked in with me and said, you know, where's the pain levels?
sentences.zh: 而且她的体谅是如此贴心，她会向我了解情况并说：“你知道的，疼痛程度怎么样？”

sentences.en: You know, do we, do we stop here?
sentences.zh: “你知道的，我们、我们到此为止吗？”

sentences.en: Do we make another day now?
sentences.zh: “我们现在改天再约吗？”

sentences.en: You know, it was really appreciated.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这真的很让人感激。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。

sentences.en: That sounds lovely.
sentences.zh: 听起来真好。

sentences.en: And I think that's, I'm going to push for a few more.
sentences.zh: 我想这也是，我打算再多争取了解一些。

sentences.en: Are there any other ways we can support friends or support maybe people in our team or our family who might maybe not even have this diagnosis yet,
sentences.zh: 还有什么其他方式可以支持朋友，或者支持我们团队或家里的那些人——他们可能甚至还没有被诊断出这种病，

sentences.en: but they are heading in that direction or do already have that diagnosis?
sentences.zh: 但他们正朝着那个方向发展，或者已经确诊了？

sentences.en: Have you got any other top tips for us, if you can think of any?
sentences.zh: 如果你能想到的话，能给我们一些其他的绝佳建议吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I would say patience is the massive top tip.
sentences.zh: 是的，我会说“耐心”是最为重要的绝佳建议。

sentences.en: You might not get a response straight away.
sentences.zh: 你可能不会马上得到回复。

sentences.en: You might not get a text back.
sentences.zh: 你可能收不到回信。

sentences.en: You might not hear from them for a while.
sentences.zh: 你可能有一段时间听不到他们的消息。

sentences.en: And knowing that that is nothing to do with you and everything to do with how their symptoms are that day, that week, patience is a huge part of it and understanding.
sentences.zh: 并且你要明白，这与你毫无关系，完全取决于他们那天、那一周的症状如何，耐心和理解是其中非常重要的一部分。

sentences.en: And asking, you know, there's nothing wrong with asking, you know, how can I help?
sentences.zh: 还有询问，你知道的，询问“我能帮什么忙？”并没有错，

sentences.en: How can we adjust this meetup, this activity?
sentences.zh: “我们该如何调整这次聚会、这次活动？”

sentences.en: You know, how do we make it different?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们该如何做出改变？

sentences.en: Do we change the place?
sentences.zh: 我们要换地方吗？

sentences.en: Do we change the time?
sentences.zh: 我们要换时间吗？

sentences.en: Because often I know my symptoms are worse in the morning than they are in the afternoon.
sentences.zh: 因为我常常知道我的症状在早上比在下午更严重。

sentences.en: So that person is the expert in themselves and what is going to happen to their symptoms and how to manage them.
sentences.zh: 所以这个人才是他们自身的专家，最清楚他们的症状会发生什么以及如何应对。

sentences.en: So just ask.
sentences.zh: 所以直接问就好了。

sentences.en: Great advice.
sentences.zh: 很好的建议。

sentences.en: And as you were talking, I was thinking, well, obviously a lot of my audience are aspiring psychologists.
sentences.zh: 而且在你说话的时候，我在想，很显然我的很多听众都是有志成为心理学家的人。

sentences.en: And I was thinking about, well, what if there's an aspiring psych or someone that wants to retrain to become a qualified psych, watching or listening to this and thinking,
sentences.zh: 我在想，如果有立志成为心理学家的人，或者想要重新培训成为合格心理学家的人，正在观看或收听这个节目，并且在思考：

sentences.en: can I do this with this diagnosis?
sentences.zh: 带着这种诊断，我能做到这一点吗？

sentences.en: But it also made me think about, I know that some courses, I think Lancaster, I know are one, are offering part-time clinical psychology doctorates now.
sentences.zh: 但这同时也让我想起，我知道有些课程，据我所知兰卡斯特大学就是其中之一，现在正提供非全日制的临床心理学博士学位。

sentences.en: So I think it equates to 0.7 rather than 1.0 whole time equivalent, and that's like four years and three months or something rather than three years.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这相当于全日制工作量的0.7而不是1.0，学制大约是四年三个月左右，而不是三年。

sentences.en: I know everyone is different, but do you think that sort of accommodation could help us to kind of get people with ME, CFS in our psychology workforce?
sentences.zh: 我知道每个人都不一样，但你认为这种体谅和调整能帮助我们把患有ME、CFS的群体吸引到我们的心理学工作队伍中来吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think any flexibility has got to be helpful.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为任何灵活性肯定都是有帮助的。

sentences.en: And also thinking about, you know, the type of caseload or thinking about, you know, even with lectures, you know, are you planning in enough breaks?
sentences.zh: 同时也要考虑，你知道的，工作量的大小，或者考虑，你知道的，甚至在听讲座时，你知道的，你是否有计划足够的休息时间？

sentences.en: Can you take yourself off somewhere to have a rest during those breaks?
sentences.zh: 在这些休息期间，你能离开去某个地方休息一下吗？

sentences.en: I know myself, when I was training, breaks were socialise, go for a walk, you know, they were filled with more activity.
sentences.zh: 我深有体会，当我还在接受培训时，休息时间就是社交、去散步，你知道的，休息时间被更多的活动填满了。

sentences.en: And so thinking about how do you plan those rest breaks into that structured day so that you can adjust your energy limits accordingly?
sentences.zh: 因此，要思考如何在结构化的一天中规划这些休息时间，以便你能相应地调整你的能量极限？

sentences.en: And it's absolutely doable because there was somebody in my year that successfully navigated training and graduating alongside ME, as difficult as I'm sure it was.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是做得到的，因为我同届里就有人在患有ME的同时，成功熬过了培训并毕业了，尽管我可以肯定这一定非常困难。

sentences.en: Not that I realised at the time.
sentences.zh: 倒不是说我当时意识到了这一点。

sentences.en: No, hindsight is 20-20 vision, as they say.
sentences.zh: 不，正如他们所说，事后诸葛亮，旁观清。

sentences.en: But yeah, certainly, I think even going on to a cohort and forming those relationships with people, that can feel like a very active process.
sentences.zh: 但是，是的，当然，我认为即使是进入一个学习群体并与人们建立这些关系，那也会感觉是一个非常积极的过程。

sentences.en: It's very engaged.
sentences.zh: 这是高度参与的。

sentences.en: And I know every time I've started a new job and a new placement, you know, or done something new, it really messes with my sleep because my brain is like fizzing with the names,
sentences.zh: 而且我知道每次我开始一份新工作和新实习时，你知道的，或者做了什么新事情，它真的会把我的睡眠搞得一团糟，因为我的大脑里充斥着各种名字、

sentences.en: with the faces, with the smells, with the people.
sentences.zh: 各种面孔、各种气味、各种人。

sentences.en: And so if already your sleep is not restful and then you're doing all of these new things, I'm guessing to use a term that I know you're familiar with and we will explain shortly,
sentences.zh: 所以如果你的睡眠本就已经无法恢复精力，然后你又在做所有这些新事情，我猜——用一个我知道你很熟悉、我们稍后会解释的词——

sentences.en: takes a lot of spoons.
sentences.zh: 这需要消耗大量的“勺子（能量）”。

sentences.en: Yes, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是的。

sentences.en: It takes an awful lot of spoons and an awful lot of planning those spoons.
sentences.zh: 这需要消耗极其大量的“勺子”，并且需要对这些“勺子”进行极大量的规划。

sentences.en: Yeah, so let's talk about spoons.
sentences.zh: 是的，那我们来谈谈“勺子”吧。

sentences.en: I know this was an idea that I think came about on social media a few years ago for thinking about managing your energy levels when you have chronic fatigue.
sentences.zh: 我知道这是一个几年前出现在社交媒体上的概念，用于思考当你患有慢性疲劳时如何管理你的能量水平。

sentences.en: But you might well know more about the origins for that and be able to talk us through it there.
sentences.zh: 但你很可能对它的起源了解得更多，并且能够为我们详细讲讲。

sentences.en: So the origins were, I'm terrible with names and my brain isn't going to let me remember them, but it was a woman who was explaining energy limiting conditions.
sentences.zh: 所以它的起源是——我对记名字实在太差劲了，我的大脑不会让我记起它们，但那是一位用来解释能量限制性疾病的女士。

sentences.en: So the idea is, is that within a day, you have a limited amount of spoons and we imagine those spoons to be units of energy.
sentences.zh: 所以这个想法是，在一天之内，你的精力是有限的，我们把这些精力想象成一个个“勺子”，即能量单位。

sentences.en: And you may wake up with less spoons than others on some days, but we certainly have a limited amount of spoons compared to somebody without an energy limiting condition.
sentences.zh: 有些日子你醒来时拥有的“勺子”可能比别人少，但与没有能量限制疾病的人相比，我们的精力绝对是有限的。

sentences.en: You then take those spoons or units of energy and you have to decide and plan your day where you are going to spend those spoons.
sentences.zh: 然后，你拿着这些“勺子”或能量单位，必须决定和规划你这一天要把这些“勺子”花在什么地方。

sentences.en: So getting up, maybe a spoon, having a spoon, maybe a spoon or two spoons, depending on the severity of your illness, taking a phone call, maybe a spoon.
sentences.zh: 比如起床可能需要一个勺子，吃东西可能需要一个或两个勺子，这取决于你病情的严重程度，接听一个电话可能需要一个勺子。

sentences.en: And it's important to recognize that it's not just about physical energy.
sentences.zh: 并且认识到这不仅仅关乎体力，这一点很重要。

sentences.en: It's also about social energy, emotional energy, mental energy and sensory energy.
sentences.zh: 它还关乎社交能量、情感能量、心理能量和感官能量。

sentences.en: So how much our environment might use those spoons also.
sentences.zh: 也就是我们的环境会消耗多少这些“勺子”。

sentences.en: And when you consider all of those things, thinking, where is the most important place to spend those spoons?
sentences.zh: 当你把所有这些因素都考虑进去时，就会思考：把这些“勺子”花在哪个地方最重要？

sentences.en: And once they're gone, they're gone.
sentences.zh: 一旦它们用完了，就真的没了。

sentences.en: Whereas with somebody who doesn't have a energy limiting condition, you might have a rest and you might have gained some spoons back.
sentences.zh: 而对于没有能量限制疾病的人来说，你休息一下可能就能恢复一些“勺子”。

sentences.en: But unfortunately, with most conditions, you don't gain them back.
sentences.zh: 但不幸的是，对于大多数病情来说，你是无法恢复它们的。

sentences.en: You are then resting until the next day where you may wake up with the same spoons, less spoons, more spoons.
sentences.zh: 然后你就要一直休息到第二天，而第二天醒来时，你拥有的“勺子”可能和昨天一样，也可能更少，或者更多。

sentences.en: You'll find out in the morning.
sentences.zh: 你到早上才会知道。

sentences.en: Oh, it's really hard to have control, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 哦，想要掌控这一切真的很难，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, it just takes a lot more thought.
sentences.zh: 是的，这只是需要更多的思考。

sentences.en: And this is very much where the idea of pacing comes in.
sentences.zh: 这就是“步调调整”（pacing）这一概念发挥重要作用的地方。

sentences.en: So pacing is a strategy where you are going to balance how you rest and how you do activity.
sentences.zh: 所以，“步调调整”是一种策略，你要平衡自己的休息方式和活动方式。

sentences.en: So again, how you spend those spoons.
sentences.zh: 也就是再次强调如何花掉那些“勺子”。

sentences.en: Otherwise, if you spend too quickly or too much, you end up in that post-exertional malaise or PEM.
sentences.zh: 否则，如果你花得太快或太多，你就会陷入活动后疲劳加剧（PEM）的状态。

sentences.en: So there is a very tricky balance of not overdoing, but also not doing too little either.
sentences.zh: 因此，这里有一个非常微妙的平衡，既不能过度劳累，但也不能做得太少。

sentences.en: And it can look like planning rest in between activity.
sentences.zh: 它可以表现为在各项活动之间安排休息。

sentences.en: It can look like breaking down a task into more manageable chunks.
sentences.zh: 它可以表现为将一项任务拆解成更容易应付的小块。

sentences.en: So even things like getting dressed in the morning, you know, first, most people just stand up and get out of bed.
sentences.zh: 比如早上穿衣服这种事，你知道的，对大多数人来说，他们直接站起来下床就行了。

sentences.en: But for a lot of people with energy limiting conditions, you might have to break that down a little bit.
sentences.zh: 但对于许多有能量限制疾病的人来说，你可能需要把这个过程稍微拆解一下。

sentences.en: You might have to sit up firSt.
sentences.zh: 你可能得先坐起来。

sentences.en: Then you might have to put your legs over the bed.
sentences.zh: 然后你可能得把腿移到床边。

sentences.en: Then you might be able to do some standing up and sitting back down.
sentences.zh: 接着你或许可以尝试站一会儿然后坐回床上。

sentences.en: Then you might be able to collect the clothes and bring them back to where you are when you're sitting down.
sentences.zh: 然后你可能能够把衣服拿过来，拿回你坐着的地方。

sentences.en: And you also might have to cancel or decline plans like we've already talked about in order to protect the energy that you have.
sentences.zh: 而且你可能还不得不取消或推掉一些计划，就像我们之前讨论过的那样，以此来保护你仅存的能量。

sentences.en: Yeah, thank you.
sentences.zh: 是的，谢谢你。

sentences.en: It's like a whole, it's a whole other world, isn't it, really?
sentences.zh: 这简直就像是另一个世界，真的，不是吗？

sentences.en: That's what I'm, that's what I'm learning.
sentences.zh: 这就是我正在了解的。

sentences.en: Before I met my father-in-law, he had had a diagnosis of ME at that time.
sentences.zh: 在我遇到岳父之前，他当时就已经被诊断出患有肌痛性脑脊髓炎（ME）了。

sentences.en: That's what he calls it.
sentences.zh: 他是这么称呼它的。

sentences.en: Or that's what he called it at that time.
sentences.zh: 或者说他当时是这么叫的。

sentences.en: But he did get better.
sentences.zh: 但他确实康复了。

sentences.en: So I've been in his life probably about 16 years, something like that.
sentences.zh: 所以我进入他的生活大概有16年了吧，差不多是这样。

sentences.en: So he got better before I met him.
sentences.zh: 所以在我们见面之前他就已经康复了。

sentences.en: Is that common or is that uncommon?
sentences.zh: 这种情况很常见还是很少见？

sentences.en: How much do people kind of, are they able to recover and be perhaps the person they used to be before this condition?
sentences.zh: 人们在多大程度上能够恢复，并重新成为得病之前的那个人呢？

sentences.en: It's tricky, really, because it's so hard to get the statistics on even a diagnosis that it's hard to get the statistics on recovery.
sentences.zh: 说实话，这很棘手，因为就连要获取某种诊断的统计数据都很难，更不用说获取康复的统计数据了。

sentences.en: From my understanding, I see an ME service.
sentences.zh: 据我了解，我在一家ME服务机构工作。

sentences.en: From my understanding, some people may have a lifelong condition.
sentences.zh: 据我所知，有些人可能会终身患病。

sentences.en: Some people may end up in sort of a leading a better life, but have a risk of relapse.
sentences.zh: 有些人可能会过上相对较好的生活，但仍有复发的风险。

sentences.en: And some people may build themselves back up to a life where they are free of symptoMs.
sentences.zh: 还有些人能够调养自己，重新过上没有症状的生活。

sentences.en: I'm not sure on the statistics of each one, because the statistics are so difficult to get hold of, of who even has ME.
sentences.zh: 我不确定每种情况的具体比例，因为很难统计到底有多少人患有ME。

sentences.en: Yeah, and I guess, you know,
sentences.zh: 是的，我想，你知道的，

sentences.en: it reminds me of that episode of Friends where Joey Tribbiani kind of can't do certain things for a period of time because he's doing a medical research thing.
sentences.zh: 这让我想起《老友记》里的那一集，乔伊·崔比亚尼因为参加了一项医学研究，在一段时间内不能做某些事情。

sentences.en: And then as soon as he can do those things, he goes back to his old ways of being.
sentences.zh: 然后一旦他能做那些事情了，他又回到了从前的生活方式。

sentences.en: And it's like, then if you didn't have an ME presentation, CFS, would you necessarily want to spend all your time filling in research about it?
sentences.zh: 这就好像是，如果你没有表现出ME或慢性疲劳综合征（CFS）的症状，你还会愿意把所有时间都用来填写关于它的研究问卷吗？

sentences.en: Or would you want to go out there and embrace the life that you've missed, you know?
sentences.zh: 还是说你会想走出去，去拥抱你错过的生活呢？

sentences.en: And I think it's, yeah, research is great so long as we can really get a sample of people.
sentences.zh: 我觉得，是的，只要我们能真正抽样调查到合适的人群，研究就是极好的。

sentences.en: But it's not it's not always easy and always possible.
sentences.zh: 但这并不总是那么容易，也并非总能实现。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: And I suppose a bit like Joey, a lot of people end up in that boom bust cycle where they feel better.
sentences.zh: 我想有点像乔伊那样，很多人最终会陷入“兴奋-崩溃”的恶性循环，他们觉得自己好些了，

sentences.en: So they do all the things that they've missed and then they really have a good time, which then leads to a crash.
sentences.zh: 于是把所有错过的事情都做了一遍，玩得很开心，但这随后就会导致病情崩溃。

sentences.en: And that's what we call the boom bust cycle.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们所说的“兴奋-崩溃”循环。

sentences.en: And it seems like, you know, if you can pace as well as you can to break that cycle, you have more of a chance at recovery.
sentences.zh: 看起来，如果你能尽最大努力做好“步调调整”来打破这个循环，你康复的机会就会更大。

sentences.en: And kind of just before we kind of start thinking about you and what you're doing at the moment, is there any medication that's helpful?
sentences.zh: 在我们开始讨论你以及你目前在做的事情之前，我想问问有没有什么药物是有帮助的？

sentences.en: Is there any evidence based approaches like therapies that actually help to move the needle on this?
sentences.zh: 有没有什么基于证据的方法，比如疗法，能够真正推动这个病情的进展？

sentences.en: Or is this all just kind of like, I don't know, I guess acceptance and kind of biding your time?
sentences.zh: 还是说这一切都只是，我不知道，我猜就是接受现实然后苦苦等待？

sentences.en: Support's tricky.
sentences.zh: 获得支持挺不容易的。

sentences.en: I suppose it depends where you live on what's going to be available.
sentences.zh: 我想这取决于你住在哪里，能获得什么样的资源。

sentences.en: I'm very lucky in that I have a local ME service that supports me.
sentences.zh: 我很幸运，当地有一个为我提供支持的ME服务机构。

sentences.en: In terms of medication, that isn't really a route that seems very popular in that it's hard to know what to medicate.
sentences.zh: 至于药物，这似乎并不是一个很受欢迎的途径，因为很难知道该用什么药来治疗。

sentences.en: And a lot of the medications that have been tried with myself don't do anything.
sentences.zh: 而且很多在我身上尝试过的药物都毫无作用。

sentences.en: But that's always going to be a personal experience, I suppose.
sentences.zh: 但我猜这总归是个人的体验。

sentences.en: There used to be a intervention called graded exercise.
sentences.zh: 过去有一种名为“渐进式运动”的干预措施。

sentences.en: And I'm bringing it up because I want people to be aware that this is not something that should be recommended.
sentences.zh: 我提起这个是因为我想让大家知道，这不应该是被推荐的做法。

sentences.en: And if you hear it from a doctor, change doctors, because it used to be an intervention where you start a small amount of exercise and you build up.
sentences.zh: 如果你从医生那里听到这个建议，请换个医生，因为它过去是一种干预方法，即从少量的运动开始并逐渐增加。

sentences.en: And the idea is, is that your body accustoms to that.
sentences.zh: 其理念是让你的身体逐渐适应这种运动。

sentences.en: But actually, what we found is that because of post-exertional malaise, where it can hit you the day after or the day after that, is it was actually making a lot of people worse.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，我们发现由于活动后疲劳加剧（PEM）——它可能在第二天甚至后天发作——这种方法实际上让很多人的病情恶化了。

sentences.en: And so it was taken out of the guidelines.
sentences.zh: 所以它被从指南中删除了。

sentences.en: But unfortunately, some people still are given it as advice.
sentences.zh: 但不幸的是，仍有一些人被给予这种建议。

sentences.en: So I'm bringing it up as a warning label that if somebody offers that as an intervention to ignore it and find somebody else.
sentences.zh: 所以我把它当成一个警示标志提出来，如果有人把这作为一种干预手段推荐给你，请忽略它并另找高明。

sentences.en: In terms of treatments, I suppose CBT can be helpful for some people.
sentences.zh: 至于治疗方法，我想认知行为疗法（CBT）对某些人可能会有帮助。

sentences.en: And I found because of my training, acceptance and commitment therapy has probably helped me a long way into adjusting, having a diagnosis.
sentences.zh: 由于我的专业训练，我发现接纳承诺疗法（ACT）在很大程度上帮助我适应了确诊这一事实。

sentences.en: But pacing is the kind of recommended intervention.
sentences.zh: 但“步调调整”才是那种被推荐的干预手段。

sentences.en: And my local ME service teaches how you do that, which is often a difficult thing to adjust to.
sentences.zh: 我当地的ME服务机构会教你如何做到这一点，而这通常是一件很难去适应的事情。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全同意。

sentences.en: Thank you for illuminating us.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你让我们大开眼界。

sentences.en: I think it's really interesting to think about what not to do.
sentences.zh: 我觉得思考“什么不该做”真的很有意思。

sentences.en: So I really like that idea.
sentences.zh: 所以我真的很喜欢这个想法。

sentences.en: It's kind of like the graded exposure thing that people talk about in CBT.
sentences.zh: 这有点像CBT中人们常说的渐进式暴露疗法。

sentences.en: But actually, we don't we don't want to do that.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，我们不，我们不想这么做。

sentences.en: We don't want to do systematic desensitization for people with with ME or CFS.
sentences.zh: 我们不想对患有ME或CFS的人进行系统脱敏治疗。

sentences.en: Very helpful to know.
sentences.zh: 了解这些真的很有帮助。

sentences.en: Could you tell us a little bit about you and what what you're doing now professionally, Beth?
sentences.zh: 贝丝，你能给我们讲讲你自己以及你现在从事的专业工作吗？

sentences.en: I can.
sentences.zh: 可以的。

sentences.en: And it's very relevant because I think if I didn't have my ME diagnosis, I wouldn't have created this new venture of life for everybody.
sentences.zh: 这非常契合主题，因为我觉得如果我没有被诊断出ME，我就不会为所有人开创这番全新的生活事业。

sentences.en: And because I was quite happy doing one to one work in my therapy clinic.
sentences.zh: 因为我以前在自己的治疗诊所里做一对一咨询，过得挺开心的。

sentences.en: And it's only when I've really had to start thinking about how I manage my energy and that I've had to reduce my caseload.
sentences.zh: 直到我真正开始思考如何管理自己的能量，不得不减少我的接诊量时，情况才发生了变化。

sentences.en: And I'm not able to see the same amount of people that I could before.
sentences.zh: 我无法像以前那样接待那么多来访者了。

sentences.en: And so it's really made me think about how do I help people in a way that protects my energy as well?
sentences.zh: 所以这真的让我开始思考，如何能在保护自己能量的同时去帮助别人呢？

sentences.en: So life for everybody isn't solely about helping people with chronic illness.
sentences.zh: 因此，“为所有人生活”（Life for Everybody）不仅仅是为了帮助患有慢性病的人。

sentences.en: It's I do share my ME experiences from time to time with it.
sentences.zh: 我在其中偶尔也会分享自己患ME的经历。

sentences.en: But it's a lot more about diet culture and about being stuck in diet culture.
sentences.zh: 但它更多的是关于节食文化以及深陷节食文化之中的问题。

sentences.en: And it teaches people to listen to and respect their body.
sentences.zh: 它教导人们倾听并尊重自己的身体。

sentences.en: And nothing teaches you faster than a chronic illness to be able to do that.
sentences.zh: 没有什么比一场慢性病能更快地教会你这一点了。

sentences.en: But life for everybody is actually about how you do that within the diet culture that we're living in.
sentences.zh: 但“为所有人生活”实际上关注的是，在我们生活的节食文化中，你该如何做到这一点。

sentences.en: So when we live in a society that accepts that there are good foods, there are bad foods, like all the fear mongering around processed foods that I'm seeing at the moment,
sentences.zh: 所以，当我们生活在一个接受“有好食物、有坏食物”的社会里——就像我目前看到的围绕加工食品的各种贩卖焦虑的言论——

sentences.en: that you have to burn off food through exercise, that you have to be thin if you're worthy or healthy.
sentences.zh: 认为你必须通过运动来消耗食物，如果你想显得有价值或健康就必须保持纤瘦。

sentences.en: And life for everybody is helping people to question some of these accepted beliefs and unlearn the myths.
sentences.zh: 而“为所有人生活”就是帮助人们性质疑这些被默认的信念，并破除这些迷思。

sentences.en: And we focus on practical tools about how to listen to your body, how to eat without guilt, how to move your body for joy rather than burning off calories and punishment,
sentences.zh: 我们专注于实用的工具，教你如何倾听身体的声音，如何毫无负罪感地进食，如何为了快乐而活动身体，而不是为了燃烧卡路里和进行自我惩罚，

sentences.en: and learning how to accept and respect the body that you're in now, even if it doesn't match this ideal that the world is telling us we should have.
sentences.zh: 并学习如何接纳和尊重你现在的身体，即使它不符合世界告诉我们应该拥有的那种理想状态。

sentences.en: Amazing.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: That sounds superb.
sentences.zh: 听起来好极了。

sentences.en: Where can people learn more?
sentences.zh: 人们可以在哪里了解更多信息？

sentences.en: If you've got social media, where's the best place to catch up with you?
sentences.zh: 如果你玩社交媒体，在哪里能最方便地找到你？

sentences.en: Yes, you can find me on Facebook at Life for Everybody.
sentences.zh: 是的，你可以在Facebook上搜索“Life for Everybody”找到我。

sentences.en: And we also have a Facebook group there where people can come in and can openly share what they're struggling with, with their food and with their body image.
sentences.zh: 我们在那里还有一个Facebook群组，大家可以加入进来，公开分享他们在食物和身体形象方面的困扰。

sentences.en: And you can also find me on Instagram under the same name, Life for Everybody.
sentences.zh: 你还可以在Instagram上用同样的名称“Life for Everybody”找到我。

sentences.en: Amazing.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: I will make sure that I link all those details in the show notes and they'll be appearing on screen for people on YouTube as well.
sentences.zh: 我一定会把所有这些详细信息写在节目简介中，它们也会在YouTube的屏幕上显示给观众。

sentences.en: And I know in business, sometimes it can be a really helpful idea to have like something really amazing as a freebie
sentences.zh: 我知道在商业运营中，有时推出一个非常棒的免费赠品是个很有用的点子，

sentences.en: so that people get a real vibe for who you are and the way that you talk.
sentences.zh: 这样人们就能真正感受到你的为人以及你说话的方式。

sentences.en: Is there anything that people who are interested can grab from you?
sentences.zh: 有什么是感兴趣的人可以从你这里免费获取的吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 对，完全有的。

sentences.en: So on my Facebook page and on the Instagram in the bio section, there is a free guide that introduces diet culture myths and how we might start to see them in our day-to-day life
sentences.zh: 所以在我的Facebook主页以及Instagram的个人简介板块里，有一份免费指南，介绍了节食文化的迷思以及我们如何开始在日常生活中注意到它们，

sentences.en: so you can start spotting them and also give some helpful hints and tips of how to start speaking more compassionately about your body.
sentences.zh: 这样你就能开始识别它们，并且它还提供了一些实用的小建议和技巧，教你如何开始用更多同理心来谈论自己的身体。

sentences.en: Sounds ideal.
sentences.zh: 听起来太理想了。

sentences.en: And I'll make sure that that link is in the description and in the show notes for this episode as well.
sentences.zh: 我也会确保这个链接会出现在本期节目的文字说明和节目简介中。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for your time.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你抽出时间。

sentences.en: This has been a fascinating, eye-opening look at all things kind of ME and fatigue for me.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这是一次引人入胜、大开眼界的体验，让我全面了解了ME和疲劳症相关的一切。

sentences.en: So thank you for illuminating us and for spending some of your spoons with us today.
sentences.zh: 所以谢谢你让我们增长见识，也谢谢你今天和我们分享了你的一些“勺子”。

sentences.en: Thank you very much for having me.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我来参加。

sentences.en: You're so welcome.
sentences.zh: 不用客气。

sentences.en: Thanks for being here.
sentences.zh: 感谢你能来。

sentences.en: Thank you so much to Beth for her time in speaking with us.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢贝丝抽空与我们交流。

sentences.en: And please do consider following Beth on her social media where she is life for everybody and grab her free resource too, which sounds brilliant.
sentences.zh: 请务必考虑在社交媒体上关注贝丝，她的账号是“life for everybody”，还可以去领取她那份听起来就很棒的免费资源。

sentences.en: If this content has resonated with you, please do start some conversations in the comments on YouTube.
sentences.zh: 如果这个内容引起了你的共鸣，请务必在YouTube的评论区开启一些讨论。

sentences.en: Please do rally around one another.
sentences.zh: 请大家务必互相支持。

sentences.en: And if this is content that resonates with you, let me know by sharing it, by watching it,
sentences.zh: 如果这些内容能引起你的共鸣，请通过分享、观看、

sentences.en: by liking it, by engaging with it, because that helps me know that you would find similar content useful in future too.
sentences.zh: 点赞和互动来让我知道，因为这能让我明白你未来也会觉得类似的内容很有用。

sentences.en: That said, I would love to know what content you would find helpful.
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，我很想知道你觉得什么内容会对你有帮助。

sentences.en: So please do make that known too.
sentences.zh: 所以请一定要让我们知道。

sentences.en: To hear other stories about clinical psychologists and other types of psychologists who have struggled with adversity and managed to get their way to be qualified,
sentences.zh: 如果你想听听其他临床心理学家以及曾与逆境抗争并最终成功获得资质的其他类型心理学家的故事，

sentences.en: please do consider checking out the Clinical Psychologist Collective book, which you can get links to in the show notes or description.
sentences.zh: 请务必查看《临床心理学家合集》（Clinical Psychologist Collective）这本书，你可以在节目简介或文字说明中找到相关链接。

sentences.en: And if you are an aspiring psychologist and you would like to get my free guide for supercharging your applications and your interviews, it's my psychology success guide.
sentences.zh: 如果你是一位有志成为心理学家的朋友，想要获取我为优化求职申请和面试准备的免费指南，那就是我的“心理学成功指南”（Psychology Success Guide）。

sentences.en: And you can get that by going along to my website, www.aspiring-psychologiSt.co.uk.
sentences.zh: 你可以登录我的网站 www.aspiring-psychologist.co.uk 来获取它。

sentences.en: Psychologists, what if you could earn money beyond trading your time for money?
sentences.zh: 心理学家们，如果你们能赚取超越“出卖时间换取金钱”的收入，会怎么样呢？

sentences.en: I'm Dr. Marianne Trent, clinical psychologist, and I've been developing passive and recurring income streams since 2019.
sentences.zh: 我是玛丽安·特伦特博士（Dr. Marianne Trent），一名临床心理学家，我自2019年以来一直在开发被动和循环收入流。

sentences.en: I have some exciting news.
sentences.zh: 我有一个令人兴奋的消息要宣布。

sentences.en: Sophie Foote's one-to-many program is now open for enrolment.
sentences.zh: 苏菲·富特（Sophie Foote）的“一对多”项目现在已经开放报名了。

sentences.en: It's designed to help you turn your expertise into scalable offers like courses, memberships, and digital products.
sentences.zh: 它旨在帮助你将专业知识转化为可扩展的产品，比如课程、会员资格和数字产品。

sentences.en: I completed the program myself in 2022 and have since supported two cohorts of psychologists through their journeys too.
sentences.zh: 我自己于2022年完成了这个项目，此后也一直支持两期心理学家学员走过他们的成长之旅。

sentences.en: And if you join through my affiliate link, you'll receive Sophie's bonuses plus my own exclusive support package at no extra coSt.
sentences.zh: 如果你通过我的联盟链接加入，你将获得苏菲的额外福利以及我个人的独家支持套餐，且无需支付额外费用。

sentences.en: That includes six months of WhatsApp support, four group masterminds, masterclasses, personalized guidance, a Fortnum and Mason treat, and a time-limited one-to-one coaching bonus.
sentences.zh: 这包括六个月的WhatsApp支持、四次小组智囊团会议、大师班、个性化指导、一份福特南-梅森（Fortnum and Mason）小食，以及限时的一对一教练指导福利。

sentences.en: Enrolment closes on Monday the 16th of November at 10pm.
sentences.zh: 报名将于11月16日（星期一）晚上10点截止。

sentences.en: Find out more via my bonus page linked in the description.
sentences.zh: 通过简介中链接的我的奖励页面了解更多信息。

sentences.en: And remember, you must purchase through my link to receive my bonuses.
sentences.zh: 请记住，您必须通过我的链接购买才能获得我的奖励。

sentences.en: I'm here if you have any questions.
sentences.zh: 如果您有任何问题，我随时为您解答。
